name: FastVideo FastH3 — video with sound, from a first and/or last frame (8 steps)
title: Start or end on your picture
summary: Give a first picture, a last picture, or both, and describe what happens: the video starts there, lands there, or travels between them, with sound. Use it to make a clip finish exactly on a poster or a frame you designed.
description:
Write a scene and get a short film back with its own soundtrack — and optionally pin how it starts, how it ends, or both.

Give a FIRST frame and the clip begins there. Give a LAST frame and it arrives there. Give both and the model travels between them, which is the way to animate between two stills. Give neither and it is plain text-to-video. A slot you leave empty is removed from the graph, so it cannot influence the result.

★ Pick the shape that matches your first frame. The model stretches the first frame to fill the video, so a portrait picture in a widescreen video comes out squashed. The LAST frame is treated differently — it is cropped to fit rather than stretched, so its shape matters less.

Write the prompt the way this model expects: bind each picture to its moment in the clip first, then describe the shot. Pictures are numbered in the order they are given, so the first frame is <Picture 1>, and the last frame is <Picture 2> when there is a first frame but <Picture 1> when it is alone.
• First frame only (the default prompt): "For the target video, at 0.00 seconds into the target video, <Picture 1> (from [Shot 1]) is fully referenced."
• Last frame only: "How the reference pictures align with the target video — <Picture 1> (from [Shot 1]) aligns with the 5.17-second mark of the target video."
• Both: "How the reference pictures align with the target video — <Picture 1> (from [Shot 1]) aligns with the 0.00-second mark of the target video; <Picture 2> (from [Shot 1]) aligns with the 5.17-second mark of the target video."
The end mark is the clip's real length: the duration is rounded up to the model's frame grid, so 5 seconds gives 124 frames, which is 5.17 s (124 ÷ 24). Then write "integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot 1] …".

Then describe camera, action and sound in that one block. Naming the audio ("we hear rain on metal, a distant siren") is what earns a deliberate soundtrack rather than an invented one. With no frames at all you can drop the binding line and write the description alone.

This is MiniMax H3 distilled by FastVideo to 8 sampling steps, so it is several times quicker than the full model. This checkpoint was not distilled for reference pictures. For several reference pictures, use the "Put your pictures in a video" card (FastH3 OmniRef, also 8 steps) or the slower, more polished Pika H3 Flex card "Make a polished film from pictures".

promptGuides.label: MiniMax H3 — official video prompt guide
promptGuides.tip: Bind each picture to its time first (a first frame at 0.00 s, a last frame at the clip's end: 5.17 s for 5 s), then write one block covering framing, camera move, action and the sound.
